title: Portal-Systemic Anastomoses: Sites and Clinical Significance
subject: Anatomy
preview: Portal-systemic anastomoses connect portal venous tributaries to systemic veins at sites such as esophagus, rectum and abdominal wall.
quickRevision: Portal-systemic anastomoses connect portal venous tributaries to systemic veins at sites such as esophagus, rectum and abdominal wall.
Esophageal varices are a potentially severe source of upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
Management depends on the cause of portal hypertension and preventive or acute bleeding pathways.

sections.title: Core biomedical mechanism
points: Portal-systemic anastomoses connect portal venous tributaries to systemic veins at sites such as esophagus, rectum and abdominal wall.
Portal hypertension may lead to gastroesophageal varices and splenomegaly.

sections.title: Clinical application
points: Esophageal varices are a potentially severe source of upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
Management depends on the cause of portal hypertension and preventive or acute bleeding pathways.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Hemorrhoids are not synonymous with rectal varices, even though both involve the anorectal region.

quiz.question: Which site is a classic portosystemic collateral pathway?
quiz.explanation: Distal esophagus. Portal-systemic anastomoses connect portal venous tributaries to systemic veins at sites such as esophagus, rectum and abdominal wall.
